guides.favoredWhen: She dodges E with W and trades on cooldowns, but you out-poke and out-teamfight. Keep E unpredictable.

keyTips.text: She dodges your E with W speed: they start every trade she wins, so vary them.
She walks up when your cooldowns are spent (about {cd:910:Q}): track your own windows.
You are immobile: position behind the team, never alone.

tips.text: Your early poke out-trades while you last-hit: max-range Q is free.
She trades only into spent cooldowns: never show the full rotation.
She sets up ganks and catches: your immobility is her window, so ward.
She avoids straight 1v1 poke trades: force them, you win poke wars.
She dodges E all game: vary it to the end.

guides.favoredWhen: Strong laner. She edges a small lead behind creeps and outscales, so snowball before she does.

keyTips.text: Strong laner you are, but she edges a small lead and outscales: play for snowball.
She stands behind creeps to block QQ: splash or wait.
She stays far when you nuke the wave: QE and EE are yours to press.

tips.text: She rushes tier-2 boots: your poke volume must land before they do.
You are weak in early skirmishes: avoid the 2v2, take the 1v1.
You are very gankable: ward and track her jungler.
She keeps the small lead growing: deny the outscale, force errors.
Snowballed plus unganked: the edger whose lead never grew loses.

guides.favoredWhen: He rushes Edge of Night and engages on spent Q or E. Vary fear timing, punish shadow poke.

keyTips.text: Your E, purple fear, is the key spell: E down means his trade, so hold it.
Your passive proc punishes closeness: zone him off it.
He engages when you use Q: spent cooldowns are his window, so stagger them.

early-lane.text: Zed often places Living Shadow before Death Mark so he can swap away from skillshots. Hold your crowd control until he has used the swap.

win-condition.text: Death Mark always lands Zed behind his target. Pre-aim crowd control and escapes behind you, not toward where he cast it.

tips.text: His WEQ from range is free damage: keep moving, never channel.
He holds max range early: distance keeps your passive offline, so push him in.
Death Mark always lands Zed behind his target. Pre-aim crowd control and escapes behind you, not toward where he cast it.
His Edge of Night rush calms the lane: end it before it lands.
Fear up plus Q up is the denial: layered cooldowns turn every trade into your poke.

keyTips.text: Plan every trade around mana, E availability against retaliation, and the resulting wave; never spend clearing and reset mana.
Pair damaging spells for Signature of the Visionary, worth most against grouped enemies.
Skip split-pushing by default with low solo-kill pressure and weak turret damage; his teamfight value runs far higher.

tips.text: In most ranged lanes, start Q and poke QQ away from the wave or near minions for area connection, or QE for instant priority.
Starting E unlocks EE poke through minions at the cost of lane priority.
Into aggressive melee champions, open E for an EQ interrupt, hold E defensively, and keep the wave near center.
At level 2, pick Q or E for damage combos or W for empowered autos and mana recovery, usually favoring Q or E without WE-less spam.
At level 3, unlock the last school and run the full spellbook, with later Q ranks adding damage.
Pressure opponents off last hits when safe, or neutralize hard lanes and farm from range while scaling.
Clear fast with QE into WE into EE only when the exposed aftermath stays acceptable.
Freeze short to farm safely when priority runs low; ahead freezes zone but should usually fund team help instead.
Build slow pushes for long recall, roam, or turret-harass windows while respecting the higher gank risk.
Build fast pushes for recall, dive, roam, or river windows, skipping them into unbreakable enemy freezes.
Carry priority into first vision and jungle help, hovering outside enemy vision so opponents must respect a fake roam.
Commit to side ganks only on highly likely plays, since Hwei trails roaming specialists there.
Collect side waves only inside vision cover, tracking timers and rotating to objectives and fights on spawn.
With Teleport, set up opposite the next objective; without it, hold the objective side for a prompt join.
Control space and movement with area effects first, then punish anyone stepping wrong.
In fights, deal QQ single-target damage, QE area slow and zoning, and EE passive triggers across several enemies.
Keep E banked for defense and spend WQ or WW to move allies or help them absorb damage.
Land R with allied control or tighter terrain against its slow flight, aiming vulnerable carries first.
Never hold R forever; its delayed blast dodges easily but the wide slow and disruption still pay even onto a frontline target.
Vary spell picks by fight, protect the immobile mage first, then punish low or separated targets.

itemization.text: Run the burn page of Deathfire Touch, Manaflow Band, Transcendence, and Gathering Storm with Presence of Mind and Legend: Haste, flexing runes by game and build.
Take Flash and Teleport standard, buffering QQ, EQ, and R with Flash.
Start Doran's Ring for lane stats, or Tear when kills look unlikely and scaling rules at the cost of early damage.
Recall for Lost Chapter when affordable for mana, AP, and haste, even ahead of a planned Seraph's build.
Turn an early recall or first blood into snowball equity with Dark Seal, upgrading to Mejai's only on built stacks.
Rush Blackfire Torch first, since its burn fits area spells and haste builds while speeding QE clearing.
Build Blackfire Torch, Spellslinger's Shoes, Shadowflame, Cryptbloom, Zhonya's Hourglass, and Rabadon's Deathcap.

Pick Sorcerer's Shoes with limited enemy resistance, Ionian boots for haste, Mercury's Treads into heavy AP or control, Swifties for kiting, and Gluttonous Greaves only as the greedier delayed scaling pick.
